bio_short: I work at the intersection of monetary policy, financial stability and macroeconomic research — currently as a Senior Economist at AMRO in Singapore, and as a Visiting Scholar at the BIS.
bio: I am a Senior Economist at the ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office in Singapore, where I work with policymakers and academics across the region and translate macro-financial analysis into policy advice. I am currently also a Visiting Scholar at the Bank for International Settlements.

My career spans international organisations, China's central bank, and the investment bank CICC — covering policy formulation, team management, and international cooperation with the BIS, IMF and major central banks. I was trained at Tsinghua University, where I read Mathematics and Physics before an M.Econ. in Finance and a Ph.D. in Economics, with research stays at Princeton and the BIS.

I am drawn to the defining questions of the field: how inflation and credit evolve, how monetary transmission works across different financial structures, and what institutions can do to preserve stability.
